content:
Sasha: Heads up — found a mismatch in the 429 handling SDK snippet in the Troubleshooting guide. The Python sample uses `retry_after` header but our SDK surfaces `retry_after_seconds` on the response object. Also the doc link anchor is broken: https://docs.redwood.ai/troubleshooting/429#retry-policies (404).
Liam: Oh huh. Which page/file is this in? can you paste the snippet that's currently in the docs?
Sasha: Current snippet in the guide: ```py
resp = client.generate(...)
if resp.status_code == 429:
    wait = int(resp.headers.get('retry_after', 1))
    time.sleep(wait)
```
Actual SDK behavior (v2.x) returns `resp.retry_after_seconds` (int) and also provides a helper `client.backoff_from(resp)`. So the snippet will silently fail if someone expects `retry_after` header key.
Maya: Yea we changed header normalization when landing SDK v2.0.4 — we normalize header names and expose `retry_after_seconds` for convenience. Docs need a migration note for v2.0.4.
Jon: I can open a PR to update the snippet + add a short migration paragraph + fix the anchor. @Sasha can you paste the minimal repro or request id (non-sensitive) so I can include a test case?
Sasha: Non-sensitive id: req-20240302-xyz. Also the anchor in the docs currently links to `#retry-policies` but the heading is `Rate limits & backoff` so the anchor mismatch is why link-check flagged it.
docs-bot: CI link-check report: docs lint check failed on master — 1 broken link detected (docs/troubleshooting/429#retry-policies). See CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/1234
Tara: For the snippet, I recommend showing the SDK helper example so folks don't re-implement header parsing. Example suggestion: ```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient, backoff_from
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate(...)
if resp.status_code == 429:
    backoff_from(resp)  # sleeps or returns backoff seconds
```
Also add an async version (`await client.backoff_from_async(resp)`).
Liam: Can we also add a short streaming example note — streaming clients should cancel and then retry with backoff instead of waiting on the streaming generator. Small snippet would help.
Jon: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 — updates Python snippet to use `backoff_from`, adds migration note for SDK v2.0.4, fixes anchor and updates the link target. Assigned reviewers: @Maya and @Tara.
Maya: I'll review today. Please also add a changelog blurb referencing SDK v2.0.4 behavior so platform teams see the change.
Sasha: Thanks — once merged can someone re-run the docs link-checker? @docs-bot :thumbsup:
docs-bot: Recheck scheduled and queued — will post results here when complete.
Liam: small nit — update the example to show tolerable max backoff (e.g., cap at 60s) and mention jitter. Otherwise looks good.
Jon: Good point, I'll add a one-liner about capping and jitter. Planning to merge after Maya approves.
Sasha: Awesome, thanks y'all — this was causing a customer repro so nice to get it fixed quickly.
